newsitem.title: USA: PacifiCorp to operate Big River plants.
newsitem.headline: PacifiCorp to operate Big River plants.

text.p: Big Rivers Electric Corp said on Wednesday that a proposal for PacifiCorp to operate the western Kentucky utility's power plant is the basis for a settlement reached with virtually all of its major creditors.

Big Rivers said its lawyers advised the U.S. Bankruptcy court a settlement has been reached, subject to certain conditions and approvals from the court and the boards of Big Rivers and the four distribution cooperatives it serves.
It said "resolving the bankruptcy issues will enable us to move forward in obtaining necessary regulatory approvals in a timely fashion for our partnership with PacifiCorp."
The Big Rivers statement quoted PacifiCorp as saying "we are confident that we can finalize our long-term arrangement by mid-year."

The parties agreeing to the settlement include the Rural Utilities Service, the largest creditor; two New York banks, who are the largest unsecured creditors; the four distribution cooperatives served by Big Rivers; the region's two aluminum smelters; and PacifiCorp and Big Rivers.
The principal points of the settlement are included in Big Rivers' bankruptcy reorganization plan submitted to the Bankruptcy Court.
A Big River spokesman said no further details on the participants in the settlement will be available until that filing has been completed.

The basis for the reorganization plan is Big Rivers' agreement with PacifiCorp to lease and operate Big Rivers' generation facilities over the next 25 years, the company said. It said PacifiCorp was selected following a competitive bid process in 1995.
In addition to court approval, the transaction must obtain regulatory approvals from the Kentucky Public Service Commission and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

Big Rivers said PacifiCorp will pay a fixed annual rental of $30.1 million and sell power to Big Rivers at $0.0192 per kilowatt hour through the year 2000. PacifiCorp will sell surplus power wholesale.
Big Rivers said it will continue to serve its four cooperative members with power purchased from PacifiCorp and provide transmission services to PacifiCorp and others.

Big Rivers provides power to Henderson Union Electric Cooperative, Green River Electric Corporation, Jackson Purchase Electric Cooperative Corporation and Meade County Rural Electric Cooperative Corporation.

The settlement also calls for the Rural Utilities Service to reduce its interest rate to 5 percent from 8.37 percent and restructure the payments on its $1.2 billion debt over the term of the PacifiCorp lease, providing significant cash flow savings to Big Rivers.

Big Rivers' member cooperatives have agreed to rates which will result in stable competitive prices for all their consumers. In addition, the aluminum smelters have agreed to new competitive rates, under contracts which run until 2010, and to terminate all litigation with Big Rivers.

The New York banks will pay Big Rivers about $14 million and be released from further obligations on their letters of credit for Big Rivers $143 million in pollution control bonds. Big Rivers will obtain replacement letters of credit and continue to pay the bonds.

Big Rivers said it can complete preparation of its regulatory filings once the replacement letter of credit has been obtained and the creditors have approved the form of the plan of reorganization and rate-case filing.
